title: Burst demux, fairshare redistribution and standby-replay orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During the 2026-01-28 outage two regional limiter replicas were briefly partitioned and a subset of tenants accumulated burst credits on the primary region while standby replicas drained. On reconnection we observed large imbalanced admission spikes and several tenant SLO breaches. We need a deterministic, auditable mechanism to demultiplex (demux) burst credits, fairly redistribute admission tokens across tenants, and safely replay queued requests from standby/standby-replay buffers during limiter rehydration so applications do not see sudden token floods or starvation.

Scope & goals:
- Design a 'burst-demux' protocol that tags and shards burst credits with an epoch and stable tenant fingerprint so redistribution can be idempotent.
- Implement a 'fairshare redistributor' in limiter coordinator that rebalances outstanding soft-credits across tenants using a weighted fair-share heuristic (weight = prod tier weight * recent usage smoothing).
- Provide a 'standby-replay orchestrator' that sequences replayed admissions through circuit-breaker and SLO-aware pacing so we never exceed per-tenant/region concurrency SLOs during catch-up.
- Integrate with multi-region failover policy: when a region fails and traffic is routed to warm standby, credits are shadowed and reconciled on regional restore.
- Add observability: per-epoch reconciliation dashboard, audit log entries for redistributed credits, and alerts when redistribution causes >10% deviation from expected steady-state.

Success criteria:
- No tenant sees >2x baseline QPS spike as a result of reconciliation in canary tests.
- Reconciliation completes deterministically within the 'reconcile window' (configurable, default 60s) and yields balanced credit distribution (Gini coefficient <0.15 for tenant share).
- Automated chaos test (partition/rejoin) shows rollout reduces historical incident recurrence rate for limiter-related SLO breaches by >=80% in simulated traffic.

Design trade-offs discussed:
- Strong consistency vs eventual reconciliation: we prioritise availability during partition by allowing temporary shadow credits and reconciling on restore instead of synchronously blocking traffic.
- Complexity of replay: strictly ordering replay per-tenant increases coordination cost; we choose per-tenant pacing tokens with global throttle guard instead of global strict ordering for simpler failure modes.
- Fairness metric: opted for weighted fair-share with exponential moving average smoothing to balance short bursts from critical tenants without starving low-traffic tenants.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged canary in staging (10% regional traffic) with detailed telemetry.
2) Expand to a handful of low-risk production tenants and run for 48h.
3) Progressive ramp to global with health gates (error rate, token surge, SLO violations).
4) Full rollout and tag release.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/LIMIT/Burst+Demux+and+Standby+Replay+Design
- Simulation harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/limiter-sim/tree/feature/burst-demux
- Incident writeup that motivated this: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Limiter+2026-01-28+Incident

Open questions:
- Should we record redistributed credits as explicit ledger entries (stronger audit) or ephemeral metrics? Ledger increases storage/IO but simplifies postmortem.
- Exact weighting formula for fairshare (we have a working heuristic; need PM signoff).
